title: Operator mentoring runloop and dark-launch exercise kit
author: Marisol Ortega
body:
SUMMARY
This page defines a repeatable operator mentoring runloop plus a companion dark-launch exercise kit that teams can use to accelerate oncall readiness. It combines a structured apprenticeship progression, short-form runbooks, measurable pass/fail criteria, and a set of reproducible simulated incidents suitable for dark-launch (internal-only) exercise windows.

PURPOSE
- Reduce time-to-solo for new oncall responders from months to weeks.
- Provide a friction-free way to validate runbooks and fallback policies before customer-visible rollouts.
- Teach escalation judgment, evidence collection, and customer communication through deliberate practice.

WHO SHOULD USE THIS
- New oncall responders (shadowing phase)
- Senior responders (mentors / evaluators)
- Team leads planning game days or pre-release dark-launches

KEY CONCEPTS
- Mentoring runloop: cyclical apprenticeship model pairing a new responder with a mentor for consecutive rotations, with defined learning objectives each shift.
- Dark-launch exercise: a controlled internal rollout of synthetic failures or traffic patterns (non-customer affecting) to validate operational controls and human runloop.
- Evidence-first triage: collect minimum reproducible evidence before taking disruptive actions.

APPRENTICESHIP PROGRESSION (4 stages)
1. Observe (2 shifts)
   - New responder shadows mentor in the bridge, observes triage decisions and comms.
   - Objective: identify primary telemetry signals for your service and list three runbook entry points.
2. Assisted Triage (3–5 shifts)
   - New responder performs triage with mentor in the bridge; mentor proposes next steps and monitors.
   - Objective: perform initial diagnosis and open a remediation ticket with evidence.
3. Guided Response (2–4 shifts)
   - New responder runs the bridge with mentor as observer, executes contained mitigations.
   - Objective: run through at least two containment actions from runbook without escalation.
4. Solo (graduation)
   - New responder leads the bridge for a full rotation; mentor available but not in the bridge.
   - Graduation criteria (all must pass): documented runbook edits made where needed, 1 mock post-incident writeup, and mentor sign-off.

MENTOR CHECKLIST (per shift)
- Pre-shift: confirm access (pager, dashboards, runbook editor).
- During shift: require evidence-before-action for stateful operations.
- Post-shift: leave a concise note in the apprenticeship log (what went well, what to practice).

RUNLOOP CADENCE
- 2-week mentoring sprint: each apprentice shadows 1 week, assisted triage the following week. Repeat until graduation.
- Monthly retro and runbook pruning session (2 hours).

DARK-LAUNCH EXERCISE KIT
Use these exercises during internal-only traffic windows (labelled "dark-launch") or scheduled game days. Each exercise includes a scenario, success criteria, scoring rubric, and safe abort conditions. Exercises are intentionally small scope (30–90 minutes).

Exercise A: KV-cache noisy neighbor
- Scenario: background synthetic tenant generates spikes that cause evictions and p99 latency increases on inference pods.
- Goal: validate auto-scaling, rapid cache-prefetch heuristics, and customer-impact detection.
- Steps:
  1) Turn on synthetic traffic generator (infra-runner playbook).
  2) Observe p95/p99 latency drift and cache-miss rate.
  3) Execute containment: temporarily isolate generator or apply rate-limit route-class B.
- Success criteria:
  - Oncall detects signal within 5 minutes.
  - Containment reduces p99 to baseline within 10 minutes.
  - Post-exercise runbook update recorded if any ambiguity was discovered.
- Abort conditions: sustained error rate > 0.5% or customer-facing status page triggers.

Exercise B: Model variant fallback failure
- Scenario: Canary rollout of a smaller quantized model variant causes intermittent decode errors.
- Goal: validate rollback and fallback routing without full rollback of serving fleet.
- Steps:
  1) Start canary with 5% traffic.
  2) Inject synthetic malformed payloads to surface decode errors.
  3) Verify automated fallback triggers and route 100% of affected traffic to stable variant.
- Success criteria:
  - Automatic fallback engages within 3 error occurrences OR manual fallback executed within 6 minutes.
  - No customer-visible error increase after fallback.

SIMULATION RUNBOOK TEMPLATE (short-form)
- TOOLS REQUIRED: k8s access, synthetic traffic generator, runbook editor, status-page draft tool.
- CONTACTS: oncall@redwood.com, infra-leads Slack #infra-ops, AM on-call.
- TELEMETRY CHECKS (minimum evidence):
  - service: inference-api - error rate (5min)
  - infra: node GPU utilization
  - cache: eviction_rate/second
  - routing: 5xx by model variant

SIMPLE TABLE: exercise schedule example
| Window | Duration | Participants | Lead | Notes |
| Dark-launch-1 | 60m | 1 mentor + 1 apprentice + infra lead | Lydia Chen | KV-cache exercise |
| Dark-launch-2 | 90m | 2 mentors + 3 apprentices | Ethan Zhao | Model fallback exercise |

EVIDENCE-FIRST TRIAGE CHECKLIST
1. Collect a timestamped chart snapshot (5min window).
2. Collect at least one request-level example (headers + payload) that exhibits failure. DO NOT SHARE customer PII; redact tokens.
3. Confirm correlated infra events (node restarts, autoscaler events).
4. Confirm whether rate-limiting or recent rollouts overlap the window.

COMMUNICATION TEMPLATES (status page & CSR)
- Status page short-form (customer visible):
  Title: Service degradation for text generation - investigating
  Impact: Customers in region us-west may experience elevated latency and occasional 5xx on text-generation endpoints.
  Update cadence: every 30 minutes until mitigated.
  Mitigation: failing traffic is isolated to a canary pool and traffic is being rerouted to a stable model variant.

- CSR script (for support reps):
  Opening: "Thanks for reporting this. Our oncall team is investigating increased latency for text generation in us-west. We have isolated the issue and are implementing a mitigation. I'll follow up with the next update in 30 minutes."
  Close: Provide ETA and post-incident follow-up link if the incident will require credits or customer remediation steps.

POST-EXERCISE POSTMORTEM CHECKLIST (template)
- Title: [exercise] KV-cache noisy neighbor - YYYY-MM-DD
- Summary: one paragraph summary of what happened.
- Timeline: bullet list of key signals, actions, and times.
- Root cause hypothesis: short paragraph.
- Corrective actions: list owner + ETA for each item.
- Runbook changes: patch link to edited runbook.
- Training action: list apprentices to re-run exercise or pair for follow-up.

ESCALATION SLIDING SCALE (decision ladder)
- Low confidence / non-service-impacting: contact mentor, track in apprenticeship log.
- Medium (customer visible latency spike): escalate to service steward and infra lead, open severity-3 incident.
- High (widespread errors / security): page SRE incident commander and execute full incident playbook.

EXAMPLE COMMANDS AND SNIPPETS
- Start synthetic generator (infra runner):
  curl -X POST https://infra-runner.internal/api/generate -d '{"profile":"kv-noisy-neighbor","scale":1000}' 

- Minimal evidence collection script (shell):
  #!/bin/bash
  echo "snapshot \$(date -u)" > /tmp/exercise-evidence.txt
  kubectl top pods -n inference >> /tmp/exercise-evidence.txt
  curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?service=inference-api&minutes=5" >> /tmp/exercise-evidence.txt

RETROSPECTIVE AND GRADING RUBRIC
- Pass: apprentice identifies the correct primary signal within 5 minutes, proposes containment action, and documents a clear remediation ticket.
- Partial: apprentice needs prompting but completes containment with mentor support.
- Fail: apprentice cannot identify the signal or executes a disruptive action without evidence.

RUNBOOK SIZING GUIDELINES (short-form)
- Keep runbook steps short (3–7 actions).
- Highlight irreversible actions (DELETE, ROLLBACK) in a red banner at top.
- Include a one-line detection rule and the minimum evidence required.

RETENTION AND LEARNING ARTIFACTS
- Apprenticeship log: each exercise must leave a short log entry in the team Apprenticeship spreadsheet (link: /team/apprenticeship).
- Recordings: bridge recordings for exercises are kept for 30 days and used for feedback.

RESPONSIBILITIES & OWNERSHIP
- Mentoring program owner: eng-sre learning lead (currently Lydia Chen).
- Tooling & infra for dark-launches: infra team (owner: Ethan Zhao).
- Runbook governance: service steward for each product service.

RELATED PAGES
- Link to oncall skill lattice and game-day catalog (see related_pages above).

APPENDIX: QUICK CHECKLIST FOR SHIFT START
- Confirm pager is reachable and silenced rules are correct.
- Open relevant dashboards and runbook pages.
- Confirm synthetic traffic windows and dark-launch schedule.

CONTRIBUTION NOTES
- To propose a new exercise, open a PR against /ops/game-day/exercises and include scenario, abort conditions, and success criteria.

END OF DOCUMENT
